# paws

> paws: run-anywhere CI/CD pipelines, backed by Dagger

paws is a run-anywhere CI/CD CLI backed by Dagger. Every subcommand below is also exposed as an MCP tool via `paws mcp serve` (see `paws mcp setup` to wire up an MCP client), calling this same code directly.

## Quickstart for an AI agent

If you're an AI coding assistant reading this file (pasted in directly, or fetched from <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mbround18/paws/main/llms.txt>) and asked to wire `paws` into the current repo, run these in order:

```sh
# 1. Install the paws binary (detects OS/arch, puts it on PATH)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mbround18/paws/main/scripts/install.sh | sh

# 2. Install dagger, which most paws subcommands need on PATH
paws init

# 3. Register paws as an MCP server for this client (writes/merges .mcp.json;
#    pass --client claude-desktop instead for Claude Desktop's global config)
paws mcp setup

# 4. Scaffold a starter GitHub Actions workflow for this repo, if it doesn't have
#    one yet (detects the repo's ecosystem(s) automatically)
paws workflow generate
```

After step 3, restart/reload the MCP client (or start a new session) so it picks up `.mcp.json` — every subcommand documented below then becomes available as an MCP tool (`paws mcp serve`), calling the same code the CLI does, not a subprocess. In CI, prefer `mbround18/paws/actions/paws-up@main` over the install script (see the "GitHub Actions" section below) — it's the same install, packaged as a composite Action.

## Configuration: `paws.toml`

Optional, at the repository root. Only needed for toolchains with no native version file, or to pin the tools `paws` itself installs and runs:

```toml
[toolchains]
ruby = "3.3.0"
dotnet = "9.0"

[tools]
dagger = "0.18.10"    # what `paws init` installs
semgrep = "1.99.0"    # the scanner images `paws audit` runs
```

`paws ci` resolves a toolchain version from, highest precedence first: `--toolchain-version`, then the ecosystem's own version file (`rust-toolchain.toml`, `.nvmrc`, `.python-version`, `.ruby-version`, `go.mod`, `.tool-versions`, ...), then `paws.toml`, then a built-in default. A native version file deliberately outranks `paws.toml`, so `paws ci` never builds against a different compiler than a local `cargo build` in the same directory. Every run prints which it used and why.

Pinning `dagger` matters more than it looks: unpinned, `paws init` installs whatever the install script currently serves, so two runs weeks apart can leave different engines behind.

## Environment variables

Inside GitHub Actions the `GITHUB_*` variables are already set; `secrets`/`vars` supply the rest.

| Variable | Read by |
| --- | --- |
| `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` | every subcommand that talks to the GitHub API, as the `--repository` fallback |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` | `semver --push`, `changelog --commit`, `helm --publish`, `release`, `docs --provider`, `llms generate --publish`, `assign`, `ci --toolchain esp32 --publish-artifacts` |
| `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (or `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`) | any of the above, in place of a token: `paws` mints a short-lived installation token itself, so no separate token-minting Action is needed |
| `GITHUB_SHA`, `GITHUB_REF`, `GITHUB_REF_NAME`, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` | `semver`, `docker`, `release`, `assign` — the ref/commit/event a build is for |
| `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`, `DOCKER_TOKEN` | `docker`, to publish to docker.io |
| `GHCR_USERNAME`, `GHCR_TOKEN` | `docker`, to publish to ghcr.io (`GHCR_TOKEN` falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`) |
| `<REGISTRY>_TOKEN` | `docker --registries`, for any other registry: the host uppercased with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by `_`, suffixed `_TOKEN` (`myco.jfrog.io` reads `MYCO_JFROG_IO_TOKEN`) |
| `PAWS_CACHE_SAVE` | `ci`/`docker`: `auto` (default — save on push/dispatch/schedule, not on pull requests), `always`/`1`, or `never`/`0` |
| `PAWS_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` | `ci`/`docker`: largest engine-state archive to upload to the Actions cache, default 104857600 (100 MiB) |
| `PAWS_UPLOAD_ARTIFACT`, `PAWS_ARTIFACT_FILENAME` | `ci`/`docker`: copy the engine-state archive into `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/paws-artifacts/` for debugging an oversized archive |
| `ACTIONS_CACHE_URL`, `ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL`, `ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN` | set by the Actions runner; what `paws cache` detects the `github-actions` backend from |

Run `paws cache --json` to see which build-cache backend would be selected right now, and why.

## Command reference

Every flag below is generated from this CLI's own `clap` definition, so it cannot drift from what the binary accepts. A flag shown as `--name <VALUE>` takes a value; one shown as `--name` is a boolean switch.

## paws ci

Build and test a language target (node, rust, python, go, java, kotlin, ruby, php, dotnet, elixir, ansible, tauri, tauri-android, flatpak, esp32)

```sh
paws ci [OPTIONS]
```

- `--source <SOURCE>` — Directory to build, relative to the current one. Defaults to the current directory
- `--toolchain <TOOLCHAIN>` (one of `node`, `rust`, `python`, `ansible`, `go`, `java`, `kotlin`, `ruby`, `php`, `dotnet`, `elixir`, `tauri`, `tauri-android`, `flatpak`, `esp32`) — Which toolchain to build. The accepted values are listed below, read from the same registry `paws ci` dispatches on — so this list cannot fall behind what the command actually supports
- `--toolchain-version <TOOLCHAIN_VERSION>` — Build against a specific version of `--toolchain`, e.g. `--toolchain rust --toolchain-version 1.90.0`
- `--verbose` — Print per-ecosystem provisioning start/elapsed timing to stderr
- `--silent` — Suppress dagger's live build progress; only print output once the pipeline finishes (or on failure). Default is streamed live
- `--targets <TARGETS>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — Cross-compile to these GOOS/GOARCH pairs instead of the native build, e.g. "linux/amd64,darwin/arm64,windows/amd64" — only valid with `--toolchain go`. Binaries land in `dist/` under the project root; `go test` is skipped for every target (none of them can run in this build container, native or not)
- `--coverage` — Also run `cargo llvm-cov` after the normal test step and print a coverage summary — only valid with `--toolchain rust`. Builds against a dedicated `builders/rust` image (pre-installed `cargo-llvm-cov`) instead of pulling `rust:1-bookworm` directly; the default (flag omitted) pipeline is unaffected. A no-op on a wasm project (`cargo test` is already skipped there for the same reason coverage can't be measured)
- `--publish-artifacts` — After a successful build, upload the built bootloader (`bootloader.bin`) and firmware ELF as assets on the GitHub Release matching the current tag (`$GITHUB_REF_NAME`) — only valid with `--toolchain esp32` (mirrors `--coverage`'s existing `--toolchain rust`-only gating). Needs `$GITHUB_TOKEN`/`$GH_TOKEN` and `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY` set — no new env var name, reusing the same convention every other GitHub-Release-touching `paws` subcommand already reads (`paws semver --push`, `paws helm --publish`). A missing token/tag fails with a clear, actionable error rather than a bare API 401. Default (flag omitted): no GitHub API interaction at all, same "additive flag changes nothing by default" shape as `--coverage`

## paws docker

Build a container image, then tag and publish it — to docker.io, ghcr.io, or any other registry. Which tags get pushed, and whether anything is pushed at all, is decided from the branch/tag/PR-label the build is running on

```sh
paws docker [OPTIONS]
```

- `--image <IMAGE>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — Image name, e.g. "ghcr.io/example/app". Falls back to `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`. A registry host here selects the registry to publish to — "ghcr.io/..." publishes to ghcr.io without also needing --registries. An unqualified name ("owner/app") is a Docker Hub reference, as docker itself reads it
- `--version <VERSION>` — Version to tag with. Falls back to `$GITHUB_SHA` (short)
- `--registries <REGISTRIES>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — Additional registries to mirror tags into, comma-separated
- `--dockerfile <DOCKERFILE>` — Path to the Dockerfile to build, relative to the repo root. Falls back to auto-detection (`Dockerfile` at the repo root, or a `compose.yml` service's own `dockerfile`/`context`)
- `--context <CONTEXT>` — Build context directory, relative to the repo root. Falls back to auto-detection alongside `--dockerfile`
- `--canary-label <CANARY_LABEL>` (default `canary`) — PR label that, when present, pushes the image for that PR build too (normally only a push to --default-branch or a tag push pushes)
- `--push` — Force push regardless of branch/tag/label gating
- `--with-latest` — Also tag and push `:latest` alongside `--version`, but only when the build is actually pushing and the ref is a real (non-prerelease) version tag — a plain branch/PR build never gets `:latest` regardless of this flag
- `--target <TARGET>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — Build a specific stage of a multi-stage Dockerfile instead of the final stage
- `--prepend-target` — Prefix the image tag with `--target`'s name, e.g. `<target>-<version>` instead of just `<version>`. Only used with `--target`, and required when several targets share one --image
- `--pr-labels <PR_LABELS>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — PR labels to check against --canary-label, comma-separated. Named `--pr-labels` to keep it distinct from `--label`, which sets OCI labels on the image itself; `--labels` still works as an alias
- `--default-branch <DEFAULT_BRANCH>` (default `main`) — The repo's default branch. A push directly to this branch, or any tag push, always pushes the image — --canary-label/--push only matter for everything else (feature branches, PRs)
- `--dockerhub-username <DOCKERHUB_USERNAME>` — Docker Hub username to authenticate publishing with. Falls back to `$DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`. Required (here or via env) to actually push to docker.io — without it the image still builds, but the push has no credentials to authenticate with and publishes nothing
- `--ghcr-username <GHCR_USERNAME>` — GHCR username to authenticate publishing with. Falls back to `$GHCR_USERNAME`. Required (here or via env) to actually push to ghcr.io. The password is read from `$GHCR_TOKEN`, falling back to `$GITHUB_TOKEN` — which is what a GitHub Actions workflow already has
- `--registry-username <REGISTRY_USERNAME>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — Username(s) for registries in --registries other than docker.io/ghcr.io (Artifactory, a private registry, etc.), as "<registry>=<username>" pairs, comma-separated — e.g. "myco.jfrog.io=deploy-bot". Any registry works here — docker.io and ghcr.io just have their own flags above because their credentials come from well-known env vars. The matching token/password is read from an env var derived from the registry: uppercased, every non-alphanumeric character replaced with `_`, suffixed `_TOKEN` — e.g. "myco.jfrog.io" reads `$MYCO_JFROG_IO_TOKEN`
- `--label <LABELS_KV>` (repeatable) — Image label as "KEY=VALUE", repeatable. Applied to the built image before it is published, which is where the OCI `org.opencontainers.image.*` set belongs — registries read `image.source` to link a package back to its repository, and an image published without it loses that link and its provenance
- `--build-arg <BUILD_ARGS>` (repeatable) — Docker build argument as "KEY=VALUE", repeatable. Merged over any build args a `compose.yml` service already declares, so a workflow can pass `GITHUB_SHA` and friends without a compose file
- `--silent` — Suppress dagger's live build/publish progress; only print output once each pipeline finishes (or on failure). Default is streamed live
- `--tag-rollup` — Also publish `major` and `major.minor` rollup tags (e.g. `:3` and `:3.2` alongside `:v3.2.1`) for release-quality version tags — the pattern consumers pinning to a major version for stability need. Gated identically to `--with-latest`: only on a real (non-prerelease) version tag build. Off by default. Similar in spirit to `docker/metadata-action`'s semver tag output, but paws's own scheme rather than a byte-for-byte match — check the tags it prints before relying on an exact equivalence
- `--version-prefix <VERSION_PREFIX>` — Prefix for the version tag and its `--tag-rollup` cascade, applied to all of them after any leading `v` is stripped from `--version`: `--version-prefix ""` publishes `:3.2.1`, `:3.2` and `:3`, and `--version-prefix v` publishes `:v3.2.1`, `:v3.2` and `:v3`. Omitted (the default), the original scheme is kept: `:v3.2.1` with unprefixed `:3.2` / `:3`. Git-sha versions keep their `sha-` tag either way
- `--no-prefix` — Shorthand for `--version-prefix ""`: publish the version tag and its `--tag-rollup` cascade with no prefix at all (`:3.2.1`, `:3.2`, `:3`). Can't be combined with `--version-prefix`
- `--tag-sha` — Also include a `sha-<sha>` tag unconditionally, alongside whatever other tags this build already produces — not only as the fallback primary tag when no version/ref-based tag applies (that fallback behavior is unaffected by this flag). Only produces a tag when `--version` is itself sha-shaped
- `--tag-branch` — On a branch-push build (not a tag, not a PR, not a scheduled run), also tag with the branch name (`/` and other non-tag-safe characters replaced with `-`)
- `--tag-pr` — On a `pull_request`-triggered build, also tag with `pr-<number>`, where the number is parsed from `$GITHUB_REF` (`refs/pull/<number>/merge`) — no separate PR-number input needed
- `--tag-schedule` — On a `schedule`-triggered build, also tag with the literal tag `schedule` (a stable, overwritable pointer, like `:latest` —  not a timestamped/nightly-dated tag)

## paws semver

Compute the next semantic version from the merged PR's labels, the branch name, or an explicit --increment. `--push` also creates the annotated tag and the matching GitHub Release

```sh
paws semver [OPTIONS]
```

- `--base <BASE>` — Base version to start from instead of the last matching tag
- `--prefix <PREFIX>` — Prefix used to filter/build tag versions, e.g. "chart-name-"
- `--increment <INCREMENT>` (one of `major`, `minor`, `patch`) — Explicit increment (major, minor, patch); skips label/branch inference
- `--major-label <MAJOR_LABEL>` (default `major`) — PR/commit label name that triggers a major bump
- `--minor-label <MINOR_LABEL>` (default `minor`) — PR/commit label name that triggers a minor bump
- `--patch-label <PATCH_LABEL>` (default `patch`) — PR/commit label name that triggers a patch bump
- `--pr-labels <PR_LABELS>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — PR/commit labels to check against major/minor/patch-label, comma-separated. Same flag name `paws docker` uses for the same thing; `--labels` still works as an alias
- `--branch <BRANCH>` (default `main`) — Branch name used for fallback inference when no configured label matches
- `--pr` — Whether this is a PR build (produces a `-pr.<sha>` prerelease)
- `--push` — Create and push the computed version as an annotated git tag, then create a matching GitHub Release with auto-generated notes (GitHub's git/tags + git/refs + releases APIs — no local git identity or worktree needed). Replaces a hand-rolled `git tag`/`git push`/`gh release create` step in the calling workflow
- `--tagger-name <TAGGER_NAME>` (default `paws-bot`) — Tagger identity attributed to the pushed tag
- `--tagger-email <TAGGER_EMAIL>` (default `paws-bot@users.noreply.github.com`) — Email attributed to the pushed tag, alongside --tagger-name

## paws init

Install the `dagger` CLI (most other subcommands need it on PATH)

## paws audit

Run the audit/compliance scanner suite

## paws docs

Build rustdoc; optionally publish it with --provider (github-pages implemented; cloudflare-pages/s3 recognized but not implemented yet)

```sh
paws docs [OPTIONS]
```

- `--provider <PROVIDER>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — Comma-delimited publish destination(s): "github-pages", "cloudflare-pages", "s3". Omitted (the default): builds target/doc locally only, nothing published — same as before this flag existed. "cloudflare-pages"/"s3" are recognized but not implemented yet (see docs/ROADMAP.md); "github-pages" publishes for real, auto-selecting the Git Trees or Pages-deployment mechanism from the repository's live Pages configuration
- `--repository <REPOSITORY>` — "owner/repo" to publish to. Falls back to `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`. Only used when --provider is given
- `--branch <BRANCH>` (default `main`) — Branch to publish to (the "github-pages" provider only). Only used when --provider includes "github-pages"

## paws provision

Provision toolchains concurrently (rust, node, python, ...)

```sh
paws provision [OPTIONS]
```

- `--toolchains <TOOLCHAINS>` (one of `rust`, `node`, `python`, `go`, `esp32`; comma-separated, or repeated) — Comma-separated ecosystems to install, e.g. "rust,node,python,go". Clap lists the accepted values from the same `Ecosystem` enum `paws provision` dispatches on, so `--help` can't fall behind what actually has an installer — a narrower set than `paws ci --toolchain`, which also builds ecosystems paws expects to already be on the runner
- `--verbose` — Print per-ecosystem provisioning start/elapsed timing to stderr

## paws helm

Lint (and optionally package) Helm chart(s) — `charts/*/Chart.yaml` or a root `Chart.yaml`

```sh
paws helm [OPTIONS]
```

- `--source <SOURCE>` (default `.`) — Host path to the source tree to scan for chart(s)
- `--package` — Also `helm package` every chart after linting, exported to `--output`
- `--output <OUTPUT>` (default `tmp`) — Host directory packaged `.tgz`s are exported to (only with `--package`)
- `--publish` — Publish: a per-chart GitHub Release (tag `<chart>-<version>`, asset uploaded only if missing) plus a real Helm `index.yaml` pushed to `--pages-branch`, so `helm repo add` against this repo's GitHub Pages URL works. Does its own packaging internally (per-chart, not the flat `--output` directory); mutually exclusive with `--package`
- `--repository <REPOSITORY>` — "owner/repo" to publish releases/index.yaml to. Falls back to `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`. Only used with `--publish`
- `--pages-branch <PAGES_BRANCH>` (default `gh-pages`) — Branch `index.yaml` is published to. Only used with `--publish`
- `--index-path <INDEX_PATH>` (default `index.yaml`) — Path to `index.yaml` on `--pages-branch`. Only used with `--publish`
- `--silent` — Suppress dagger's live build progress; only print output once the pipeline finishes (or on failure). Default is streamed live

## paws release

Cross-target build, package, and publish a release binary to GitHub Releases

```sh
paws release [OPTIONS]
```

- `--target <TARGET>` — Rust target triple to build, e.g. "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu". Must be one of `paws_release::known_targets()` — each maps to a `./builders/<dir>` Dockerfile the build runs through Dagger
- `--list-targets` — Print every target triple `paws release` knows how to build, one per line, and exit
- `--source <SOURCE>` (default `.`) — Host path to the source tree to build
- `--package <PACKAGE>` (default `paws-cli`; comma-separated, or repeated) — Cargo package(s) to build, comma-separated (one [[bin]] each) — e.g. "agent,server". Paired 1:1 with --binary-name
- `--binary-name <BINARY_NAME>` (default `paws`; comma-separated, or repeated) — Binary name(s) as declared in each package's [[bin]] section, comma-separated, paired 1:1 with --package. All built binaries are packaged into one archive
- `--local-build` — Build locally via Dagger's `docker-build` against paws's embedded generic Rust-Linux builder instead of pulling paws's own prebuilt builder image. Use this outside paws's own repo (e.g. a target repo with no `builders/` directory) — only `paws_release::local_build_targets()` are supported
- `--tag <TAG>` — Release tag, e.g. "v0.0.1-prerelease.1". Falls back to `$GITHUB_REF_NAME`
- `--prerelease` — Mark the GitHub Release as a prerelease
- `--repository <REPOSITORY>` — "owner/repo". Falls back to `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`
- `--no-upload` — Build and package only; skip the GitHub upload
- `--skip-smoke-test` — Skip the post-build smoke test (not recommended — it's what catches a binary that builds but doesn't actually run)

## paws mcp

Model Context Protocol integration: expose every `paws` subcommand as an MCP tool, calling the same Rust code the CLI calls — not a CLI subprocess proxy

## paws mcp setup

Write/merge an MCP client config so `paws mcp serve` is discoverable

```sh
paws mcp setup [OPTIONS]
```

- `--client <CLIENT>` — Which MCP client config to write/merge into: "claude-code" (default, project-local `.mcp.json`) or "claude-desktop" (global, platform-specific `claude_desktop_config.json`)

## paws mcp serve

Run the MCP server (stdio transport). Exposes every `paws` subcommand as an MCP tool by calling this crate's `run_*` functions directly

## paws llms

Generate `llms.txt`, a machine-readable summary of `paws`'s own tooling surface (see <https://llmstxt.org>)

## paws llms generate

Generate `llms.txt` from this CLI's own `--help` metadata

```sh
paws llms generate [OPTIONS]
```

- `--output <OUTPUT>` (default `llms.txt`) — Path to write the generated file to
- `--publish` — After generating, commit the file to GitHub via the Contents API (reuses `paws_release::GitHubReleaseClient`, the same mechanism `paws helm --publish` uses for `index.yaml` — no local git identity needed). Skips the commit if the generated content is unchanged
- `--branch <BRANCH>` (default `main`) — Branch to publish to. Only used with `--publish`
- `--repository <REPOSITORY>` — "owner/repo" to publish to. Falls back to `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`. Only used with `--publish`

## paws workflow

Generate a starter CI workflow for a *consumer* repo: detects its ecosystem(s) and emits a workflow wiring in `paws-up` plus the matching `paws` subcommands

## paws workflow generate

Detect this repo's ecosystem(s) and generate a starter CI workflow

```sh
paws workflow generate [OPTIONS]
```

- `--provider <PROVIDER>` (default `github`) — Which CI origin to generate for. Only "github" is implemented today — more origins (e.g. "gitlab") are planned; this keys off the same idea as `paws_environment::Provider` (currently GitHub-only too) rather than a separate abstraction
- `--output <OUTPUT>` (default `.github/workflows/paws.yml`) — Path to write the generated workflow file to

## paws auth

Credential helpers — mint tokens `paws` (or other tools) can use

## paws auth github-app

Mint a GitHub App installation access token and print it to stdout (nothing else goes to stdout, so `TOKEN=$(paws auth github-app)` works as a shell capture) — the same mechanism `actions/create-github-app-token` provides as a separate Action, done natively so no extra CI step is needed. Every other `paws` subcommand that needs a GitHub token (`semver --push`, `helm --publish`, `release`, `llms generate --publish`) already picks up App auth automatically via the same `$GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`/ `$GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` env vars — this subcommand exists for cases that want the raw token directly (e.g. handing it to another tool)

```sh
paws auth github-app [OPTIONS]
```

- `--client-id <CLIENT_ID>` — The GitHub App's Client ID (the `Iv23...`-style string). Falls back to `$GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`
- `--private-key <PRIVATE_KEY>` — The GitHub App's private key, PEM-encoded, given directly. Falls back to `$GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Mutually exclusive with --private-key-file in practice — if both are given, the file wins
- `--private-key-file <PRIVATE_KEY_FILE>` — Path to a file containing the GitHub App's private key. Falls back to `$GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`
- `--repository <REPOSITORY>` — "owner/repo" the App is installed on. Falls back to `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`

## paws publish

Publish a package to its registry (`--target rust-crate` for crates.io today)

```sh
paws publish [OPTIONS]
```

- `--target <TARGET>` — Publish target — only "rust-crate" today (crates.io or another Cargo registry)
- `--source <SOURCE>` — Path to the package to publish. Defaults to the current directory
- `--registry <REGISTRY>` — Registry to publish to. Defaults to crates.io
- `--dry-run` — Build/test/package only — skip the actual publish step. Useful for verifying a package is publish-ready without a registry token
- `--silent` — Suppress dagger's live build progress; only print output once the pipeline finishes (or on failure). Default is streamed live

## paws changelog

Generate a `CHANGELOG.md` entry from the commit/PR history between two refs. Runs standalone (e.g. to preview an entry before tagging) or chained after `paws semver --push`; `--commit` writes it back to the repo

```sh
paws changelog [OPTIONS]
```

- `--version <VERSION>` (required) — The version this changelog entry is for, e.g. "v1.3.0"
- `--previous-ref <PREVIOUS_REF>` — Overrides the auto-resolved previous ref/tag that starts the commit range. Falls back to the same prefix-aware last-tag resolution `paws semver` already implements (see --prefix)
- `--prefix <PREFIX>` — Prefix used to filter/resolve the previous tag, e.g. "chart-name-" — same meaning as `paws semver --prefix`, only used when --previous-ref is omitted
- `--output <OUTPUT>` (default `CHANGELOG.md`) — Path to the target CHANGELOG.md, relative to the current directory
- `--commit` — Also commit the updated CHANGELOG.md back to --branch via the GitHub Contents API, with a commit message carrying a `[skip ci]` loop-avoidance marker. Off by default — without this flag, only the local file is written (and the rendered entry printed to stdout)
- `--repository <REPOSITORY>` — "owner/repo" to operate against. Falls back to `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`
- `--branch <BRANCH>` (default `main`) — Branch to commit to. Only used with --commit

## paws cache

Reports which Dagger build-cache backend (`dagger-cloud`, `github-actions`, or none) `paws ci`/`paws docker` would select right now, and why — the same detection they use internally, not a separate guess. `--json` for scripting (e.g. a CI step asserting the expected backend actually activated, without grepping build log text for it)

```sh
paws cache [OPTIONS]
```

- `--json` — Print machine-readable JSON instead of the human-readable summary — `{"backend": "...", "api_version": "...", "base_url": "..."}` (`api_version`/`base_url` omitted for `dagger-cloud`/`none`)

## paws assign

Assign an issue or pull request to its owners from `CODEOWNERS`: a PR goes to the owners of the files it changes, an issue to the owners of the catch-all `*` rule. GitHub has no default-assignee setting, and `CODEOWNERS` alone only requests reviews

```sh
paws assign [OPTIONS]
```

- `--number <NUMBER>` — Issue or pull request number. Falls back to the one the triggering GitHub Actions event is about (read from `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`)
- `--assignees <ASSIGNEES>` (comma-separated, or repeated) — Logins to assign, comma-separated, instead of reading `CODEOWNERS`
- `--force` — Add owners even when the issue or PR already has assignees. Off by default so a manual assignment is never piled onto
- `--skip-bots` — Leave issues and PRs opened by bots (Renovate, Dependabot) unassigned
- `--dry-run` — Print who would be assigned without assigning anyone
- `--repository <REPOSITORY>` — "owner/repo" to operate against. Falls back to `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY`

## GitHub Actions

paws also ships composite GitHub Actions for wiring into a *consumer* repo's own CI/CD, separate from the CLI subcommands above — `paws workflow generate` scaffolds a starter workflow using these automatically.

### paws-up

Downloads a paws release binary for the current runner, puts it on PATH, and installs the dagger CLI via `paws init` (most paws subcommands need it). Composite (not Docker-based) so paws's own Dagger calls talk to the runner's real Docker daemon directly, with no Docker-in-Docker nesting. Also exposes the GitHub Actions cache runtime vars (via a pinned `actions/github-script` step) so `paws docker`/`paws ci`'s Dagger build cache can actually activate - the one non-`paws` action dependency this composite carries.

```yaml
- uses: mbround18/paws/actions/paws-up@main
  with:
    github-token: ${{ github.token }}
    install-dagger: true
    version: latest
```

**Inputs**

- `github-token` (optional, default: `${{ github.token }}`) — Token used to query/download releases (avoids low anonymous rate limits).
- `install-dagger` (optional, default: `true`) — Also run `paws init` to install the dagger CLI, which most paws subcommands need on PATH. Set to "false" to skip if the runner already has it (e.g. a self-hosted runner with dagger pre-installed).
- `version` (optional, default: `latest`) — paws version to install, e.g. "v0.0.1-prerelease.1". Defaults to the most recent GitHub Release (prereleases included — this is meant for fast dogfooding iteration, not just stable pins).

**Outputs**

- `version` — The resolved paws version that was installed.
